name: Begonia Rose
lede: Begonia Rose is a bright coral-pink named for the flower, cataloged four times over in our library yet found almost nowhere in our painting archive.

sections.title: Four catalogs, one color
sections.body: The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as "moderate red," block 15 [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas separately places it on plate I, hue 1, tone b [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also records it, and Japan's traditional color list carries the same measured hue as 薄紅, romanized Usubeni, meaning pale crimson dye [1]. Despite four independent catalogs agreeing on the hue, its nearest named library neighbor is [[ultra-red]], a notably different shade, which says more about how few true near-matches exist in our list than about any closeness between the two [2]. Our library's other near matches, [[fiery-rose]], [[red-plum]] and [[red-plum]], are all farther off, which says more about the gaps in our naming list near this hue than closeness between them [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Begonia Rose in only 1 of 23,781 paintings, essentially absent, as photographed [3]. A bright, saturated coral like this rarely survives in old pigments or varnished paint, which is likely why painters' palettes leave it almost untouched here, though that is our inference, not a measured cause [3].
